ta.name: Thematic Analysis
ta.note: A general TA orientation, not a declared subtype. Document your chosen approach; reflexive TA is one approach within the family.

steps.title: Engage with source
steps.detail: Read and revisit the full material; record your analytic position.

steps.title: Code passages
steps.detail: Link precise excerpts to researcher-defined codes.

steps.title: Develop candidate themes
steps.detail: Explore patterns of meaning across the coded material.

steps.title: Review with full source
steps.detail: Reconsider candidate themes against excerpts and wider context.

steps.title: Define themes
steps.detail: Clarify the scope, central meaning and names of the themes.

steps.title: Write with evidence
steps.detail: Develop the narrative with quotations and contextual interpretation.

references.title: Braun and Clarke · reflexive TA guidance (one TA approach)

content.name: Qualitative Content Analysis
content.note: Content analysis is a complete method. It is not a compulsory preliminary stage for TA or Comparative QCA.

steps.title: Declare unit and approach
steps.detail: Document what is analysed and the chosen content analysis approach.

steps.title: Select meaning units
steps.detail: Identify relevant passages while retaining their surrounding context.

steps.title: Condense when appropriate
steps.detail: Shorten meaning units only when this fits the analytic design.

steps.title: Code and review categories
steps.detail: Compare codes and refine categories with explicit analytic decisions.

steps.title: Interpret in context
steps.detail: Consider meaning and abstraction; themes are optional, design-dependent.

steps.title: Write with evidence
steps.detail: Connect categories, interpretation and source quotations in the report.

references.title: Graneheim and Lundman (2004) · concepts and procedures

comparative.name: Qualitative Comparative Analysis
comparative.note: Binary crisp-set, conservative, no logical remainders. Set relations do not establish causal proof.

steps.title: Define cases and sources
steps.detail: Declare the case unit and map each case to its source records.

steps.title: Define conditions and outcome
steps.detail: Document each set definition and explicit membership rules.

steps.title: Calibrate explicit 0 or 1
steps.detail: Record researcher judgments, reasons and evidence; missing is not zero.

steps.title: Review truth table and thresholds
steps.detail: Inspect all configurations, mixed outcomes and declared cutoffs.

steps.title: Conservative configurations and necessity
steps.detail: Use eligible observed configurations; no logical remainders.

steps.title: Check cases and write
steps.detail: Review cases and counterexamples before interpreting set relations.
